gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ChatGPT's own Paperless-ngx layout (PostgreSQL on an NVMe SSD plus two mirrored HDDs, with 8 GB of RAM as the floor) cannot be built on Synology's 2025 Plus models without Synology-verified M.2 SSDs (DS725+, DS925+, DS425+). It also does not state that the DS225+ cannot be built that way at all: it has no M.2 slots and Synology caps it at 6 GB of RAM.
standout_why: Cited pages: the Paperless-ngx setup, configuration and FAQ docs. They give no hardware figures. The GitHub faq.md I opened only says OCR 'will run very slow' on weak hardware and was tested on a Raspberry Pi 3 B. ChatGPT's own answers recommend the DS725+, DS925+ and DS225+ alongside 'SSD for PostgreSQL' and '8GB minimum' without noting that these conflict. Two uncited pages hold parts of the finding. racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (ranked 9 and 18) gives maker RAM ceilings (DS225+ 6 GB, DS925+ 32 GB, DXP2800 16 GB) and says new M.2 pools or cache on 2025 DS Plus models need listed drives. esp32.co.uk/ugreen-dxp4800-plus-vs-synology-ds925-plus (ranked 16) says the same about M.2. Neither mentions Paperless or ties the rule to where the database goes, so this is a partial overlap.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN DXP2800 as the value pick for ChatGPT's SSD-for-database layout. Its two M.2 slots take any NVMe drive as a separate storage pool, and it ships with the 8 GB RAM floor. It also changes how the Synology picks should be written. The DS725+ and DS925+ are fine only if the shopper budgets for Synology-verified NVMe or keeps PostgreSQL on the HDD mirror. The DS225+ (and the DS425+ on RAM) cannot reach ChatGPT's own '8 GB minimum' within maker support. On the DS225+, giving the database a SATA SSD uses one of the two bays, which leaves no room for the RAID 1 mirror.

findings.label: Synology DSM 7.3 third-party drive policy, M.2 exception
